problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $Y$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(y)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(\frac{1}{2}\le Y\le \frac{3}{2}).$

| $y$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ | $\frac{3}{2}$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(y)$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ | $0.8$ | $1.0$ |
worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $Y$ is a function $F(y)$ such that

$$
F(y)=P(Y\le y).
$$

To compute the probability of a random variable $Y$ over an interval, we can use the rule

$$
P(a<Y\le b)=F(b)-F(a).
$$

Here, we want to compute $P(\frac{1}{2}\le Y\le \frac{3}{2}).$ However, this interval is stated in the form $a\le Y\le b,$ not $a<Y\le b.$

So first, we must convert the interval $\frac{1}{2}\le Y\le \frac{3}{2}$ to the form $a<Y\le b.$ Looking at the given possible values of $Y,$ we see that $\frac{1}{2}\le Y$ is equivalent to $0<Y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{1}{2}\le Y\le \frac{3}{2}) & =P(0<Y\le \frac{3}{2}) \\  & =F(\frac{3}{2})-F(0) \\  & =0.8-0.1 \\  & =0.7.\end{aligned}
$$
